claims.quote: Tay-Sachs disease (TSD) is a fatal lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the HEXA gene which impair B-hexosaminidase A activity and result in the toxic accumulation of GM2 gangliosides.
Tay-Sachs disease (TSD) is a fatal lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the HEXA gene which impair B-hexosaminidase A activity and result in the toxic accumulation of GM2 gangliosides.

Here, we report the generation of a novel mouse model that harbors a partially humanized Hexa gene carrying c.1278insTATC, the most prevalent TSD-causing variant, and a Neu3 deficiency to circumvent a murine bypass pathway.

claims.object_mention: GM2 deposition in the central nervous system
claims.quote: Upon characterization, this model reflects key pathological features of TSD including significant GM2 deposition in the central nervous system (CNS), prominent astrogliosis, neuroinflammation, and exhibit progressive neurobehavioral impairments.
